title: Education can become a form of civic and legal capability when people need to navigate justice systems that are increasingly hard to access
source_unit: UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report and Namati, Education and justice: Learning to build just societies
geography: Global justice systems, education systems, disadvantaged populations, communities, and institutions concerned with rights, peace, democracy, and social cohesion

denominator.unit: global legal-needs and access-to-justice synthesis frame

people_without_meaningful_access.unit: people estimated to lack meaningful access to justice because they cannot resolve everyday legal problems

pressure_pattern.value: inequality, discrimination, conflict, and climate-related pressures intensify justice challenges

institutional_trust.value: low trust in justice-system institutions and actors is identified alongside declining rule-of-law conditions in many countries

observations.method: UNESCO GEM and Namati synthesis of justice needs, rule-of-law conditions, education, human rights, and people-centred justice pathways.
observations.uncertainty: The global estimate is a report-level synthesis rather than a single harmonized respondent file; it does not identify every legal problem, jurisdiction, or resolution pathway.
observations.subgroup: Disadvantaged populations, people facing discrimination or conflict, children and families, communities exposed to climate pressure, and users of justice systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Justice challenges are not uniform and legal capability, community-based support, public services, and institutional reform can improve access without assuming courts alone are the solution.

rights_understanding.value: education can help people understand their rights, navigate justice systems, and shape fairer societies

citizen_capability.value: people-centred justice requires a legally empowered citizenry

education_role.value: formal and non-formal education are treated as routes to rights awareness, participation, and social cohesion

observations.method: UNESCO/Namati analysis connecting education's moral, civic, and practical purposes with legal empowerment and people-centred justice.
observations.uncertainty: Rights literacy does not guarantee representation, remedy, institutional responsiveness, or equal treatment; the report does not claim education alone resolves legal exclusion.
observations.subgroup: Students, adults outside formal schooling, educators, community organizations, legal-aid users, and groups with limited institutional access.
observations.counterinterpretation: Legal capability can be built through community organizations, public legal services, accessible information, and collective action as well as through schools.

denominator.unit: UNESCO/Namati education and justice-system capacity frame

professional_formation.value: education has a role in developing the professional capacity of justice-system actors

system_link.value: education, legal institutions, human-rights protection, and trusted public systems are treated as interdependent

implementation_boundary.value: knowledge and training must connect to accessible, accountable, and trusted institutions to affect everyday justice

observations.method: UNESCO/Namati synthesis of formal and non-formal education, justice-system actors, legal empowerment, and people-centred institutional design.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not provide a universal causal estimate for training effects on case outcomes or institutional trust across jurisdictions.
observations.subgroup: Justice professionals, educators, legal-aid providers, community advocates, courts, administrative agencies, and people seeking remedies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional reform, funding, independence, translation, accessibility, and community support may matter as much as professional education.

observations.period: 2026; education, democracy, peace, crime reduction, and social cohesion

pathways.value: the report examines links between education and democracy, peace, and crime reduction

social_cohesion.value: education is positioned as one contributor to fairer societies and stronger social cohesion

causal_limit.value: education is not presented as a sufficient condition for justice, peace, democracy, or crime reduction

observations.method: UNESCO/Namati thematic synthesis of education's relationship to justice, democracy, peace, crime reduction, rights, and social cohesion.
observations.uncertainty: These are interconnected pathways and policy questions, not a single cross-national causal effect or forecast of political behaviour.
observations.subgroup: Learners, communities, justice institutions, civic organizations, policymakers, and populations affected by conflict or discrimination.
observations.counterinterpretation: Education can also reproduce exclusion or official narratives unless curricula, institutions, and participation are inclusive and accountable.

related_sources.claim: Namati is the justice-sector partner identified by UNESCO for the publication.
UNESCO GEM 2026 provides complementary access, equity, and education-system context.

boundary: This record adds an education-to-justice route across legal capability, rights literacy, institutional trust, professional capacity, democracy, peace, crime reduction, and social cohesion. It uses UNESCO/Namati report synthesis, not respondent-level legal histories, individual case files, courtroom outcomes, causal education estimates, or proof that schooling alone produces justice.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNESCO GEM and Namati Education and justice page reviewed for the publication title, global access-to-justice estimate, rule-of-law and trust framing, legal empowerment, professional capacity, and democracy/peace/crime pathways.
